questions.question: Why should a patient with diabetes receive retinal screening even when visual acuity seems normal?
choices: Sight-threatening retinopathy can be asymptomatic until advanced
Vision complaints always occur before retinal damage
Screening is only for patients with eye pain
Retinopathy is diagnosed by glucose alone
questions.explanation: Diabetic retinopathy and macular edema may progress without symptoms. Validated screening and comprehensive eye examinations allow treatment before avoidable vision loss occurs.

questions.question: When is the initial comprehensive dilated eye examination generally recommended for adults with type 2 diabetes?
choices: At the time of diabetes diagnosis
Only after ten years of symptoms
Only when vision becomes blurry
Never if A1c is at goal
questions.explanation: Retinopathy can already be present at recognition of type 2 diabetes, so initial dilated eye assessment is generally recommended at diagnosis, followed by interval based on results and eye-care guidance.

questions.question: Which symptom pattern requires urgent eye or emergency evaluation?
choices: Sudden flashes, many new floaters, and a curtain-like visual field loss
Stable need for reading glasses over years
Mild chronic dry eye without visual change
A normal retinal screening result last year
questions.explanation: Flashes, a shower of new floaters, and a curtain or shadow can suggest retinal tear or detachment and require urgent evaluation. Diabetes does not make this a routine outpatient symptom.

questions.question: A patient has sudden visual change with facial droop and arm weakness. What is the immediate priority?
choices: Emergency evaluation for possible stroke
Routine diabetes eye screening
Scheduling optometry in six months
Changing a glucose monitor
questions.explanation: Visual symptoms with focal neurologic deficits may indicate stroke. Emergency response takes priority over a chronic diabetic-retinopathy framework.

questions.question: What is the role of retinal photography or validated remote-reading programs?
choices: They can expand access to screening but abnormal or poor-quality results still need appropriate eye-care follow-up
They permanently replace all comprehensive eye examinations
They diagnose every cause of vision loss
They remove the need to document results
questions.explanation: Validated retinal photography can improve screening access. It does not eliminate the need for comprehensive exams, specialist follow-up, or urgent assessment of symptoms.

questions.question: Which focused history is most important for new visual symptoms?
choices: Onset, one or both eyes, field loss, pain, redness, flashes, floaters, trauma, headache, and neurologic symptoms
Only the patient’s last A1c
Only family history of glasses
Only whether the patient has diabetes
questions.explanation: Time course and associated symptoms guide the differential and disposition. New visual complaints must not be automatically attributed to diabetic retinopathy.

questions.question: Why is pregnancy an important context in diabetes eye care?
choices: Retinopathy may progress or worsen and requires coordinated preconception or pregnancy eye-care planning
Pregnancy eliminates retinal risk
Pregnancy makes eye examination impossible
Retinal screening is never needed in pregnancy
questions.explanation: Pregnancy can affect retinopathy progression in patients with preexisting diabetes. Coordinated obstetric, diabetes, and eye-care planning is important.

questions.question: Which condition is NOT safely excluded by the fact that a patient has diabetes?
choices: Retinal detachment, vascular occlusion, glaucoma, optic disease, or stroke
Only diabetic retinopathy
All eye emergencies
All medication effects
questions.explanation: Diabetes raises microvascular risk but does not explain every visual complaint. Sudden, painful, field-loss, or neurologic symptoms require a broader urgent differential.

questions.question: What is the appropriate FNP role after an abnormal retinal screening result?
choices: Ensure prompt eye-care referral, communicate results, address access barriers, and track completion
Assume the eye-care system will contact the patient
Repeat the same screen indefinitely without referral
Ignore the result if the patient has no symptoms
questions.explanation: Primary care must close the loop on abnormal screening. Timely specialist assessment and documented follow-up are necessary to prevent loss to care.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects longitudinal prevention of diabetic eye disease?
choices: Glycemic, blood-pressure, and lipid management can reduce or slow risk but do not replace eye-care screening and treatment
Good glucose control means retinal exams are unnecessary
Only insulin affects retinal outcomes
Vision loss is unavoidable in diabetes
questions.explanation: Metabolic and vascular risk reduction supports retinal health, but screening and ophthalmic assessment remain essential because retinopathy can be asymptomatic and may require eye-directed treatment.
